verdict.rationale: dlt is an open-source Python framework for building custom sources. Its declarative REST API source lets you define endpoints, relationships, pagination and authentication for any REST API, and dlt-init-openapi generates pipelines from OpenAPI specs. No fork is needed, and community reports confirm it simplifies work with small, long-tail APIs. Missing for 10: hands-on evidence of the declarative config handling non-standard auth or pagination edge cases on an API without an OpenAPI spec.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I build a custom connector for a long-tail API with a supported framework or low-code builder, not a fork

citations.quote: Using a declarative configuration, you can define: the API endpoints to pull data from, their relationships, how to handle pagination, authentication.
You can use the REST API source to extract data from any REST API.
dlt-init-openapi generates code from an OpenAPI spec that you can use to extract data from a rest_api into any destination
will greatly simplify the life of everybody dealing with small APIs that follow the OpenAPI standards.
